steps: IM ADRENALINE 0.5 mg (0.5 mL 1:1000) into anterolateral thigh — repeat every 5 min as needed. FIRST and most important step.
Remove trigger; lie flat with legs raised (sit up if breathing difficulty); high-flow oxygen.
IV fluid bolus for hypotension; nebulised salbutamol for bronchospasm.
Refractory: IV adrenaline infusion in a monitored setting.
Observe 6–12 h (biphasic risk); prescribe adrenaline auto-injector + allergy referral.

drugRefs.why: First-line and most time-critical agent — reverses airway oedema, bronchospasm and vasodilatory shock. Paediatric dose is weight-based via the paediatric formulary.

refs: Harrison's Principles of Internal Medicine, 22e — Anaphylaxis

drugRefs.why: Corrects distributive hypotension from capillary leak; large volumes may be required.
Persistent bronchospasm not resolved by adrenaline.
For anaphylaxis refractory to repeated IM adrenaline; requires haemodynamic monitoring.

drugRefs.regimenLabel: Corticosteroid (second-line, not a substitute for adrenaline)
drugRefs.why: Second-line; does not treat the acute event and must never delay adrenaline. Deemphasised in recent guidance.
Relieves cutaneous symptoms (urticaria/itch) only; not life-saving and must not delay adrenaline.

refs: Harrison's Principles of Internal Medicine, 22e — Anaphylaxis

confirm: Acute onset of airway/breathing/circulation compromise ± urticaria/angioedema after an allergen exposure.
disposition: Admit/observe 6–12 h (biphasic risk); refractory → ICU. Discharge with adrenaline auto-injector + allergy referral.
references: Harrison's Principles of Internal Medicine, 22e — Anaphylaxis
